snapshots.name: Aeneas
snapshots.body: A Trojan prince, son of the mortal Anchises and the goddess Venus, who escapes the burning ruin of Troy with his father, son, and a band of survivors. He is destined, though he does not yet know how, to found the people from whom Rome will one day rise.

snapshots.name: Dido
snapshots.body: Queen of Carthage, herself an exile who fled her home after her brother murdered her husband. She rules a city still under construction when the storm-driven Trojan fleet washes up on her shores.

snapshots.name: Turnus
snapshots.body: Prince of the Rutulians and a suitor for the hand of the Latin princess Lavinia. He resents the arrival of the Trojan newcomers as a threat to a match he considers already his.

snapshots.name: Anchises
snapshots.body: Aeneas's aged father, once loved by the goddess Venus, carried from burning Troy on his son's shoulders. He accompanies the fleet as its elder and counselor for as long as his failing strength allows.

snapshots.name: Venus
snapshots.body: Goddess of love and Aeneas's mother, who watches over her son's fortunes at every turn of his voyage. She intercedes with the king of the gods on his behalf and appears to Aeneas herself in disguise.

snapshots.name: Juno
snapshots.body: Queen of the gods, whose enmity toward the Trojans predates the poem itself and drives much of its action. She schemes throughout to delay or destroy Aeneas's fated mission to found a new home in Italy.

snapshots.name: Jupiter
snapshots.body: King of the gods, whose decrees ultimately govern Aeneas's fate despite Juno's opposition. He reassures Venus of the greatness promised to her son's descendants.

snapshots.name: the Sibyl
snapshots.body: The prophetess of Cumae, an oracle of Apollo who guides Aeneas on his journey into the underworld to seek his father. Her cryptic utterances and fierce authority mark her as no ordinary priestess.

snapshots.name: Pallas
snapshots.body: The young son of King Evander, sent by his father to fight alongside Aeneas against the Latins. His inexperience in war is matched by his eagerness to prove himself.

snapshots.name: Evander
snapshots.body: A Greek-born king who has settled and built a modest city on the future site of Rome. He welcomes Aeneas as a guest and ally and sends his own son to fight at the Trojans' side.

snapshots.name: Camilla
snapshots.body: A warrior maiden of the Volscians, raised from infancy to the life of a huntress and fighter. She leads her own troops into the war on the side of Turnus and the Latins.

snapshots.name: Creusa
snapshots.body: Aeneas's first wife, mother of his son Ascanius, lost amid the chaos of Troy's final night. Her fate haunts Aeneas even as he sails on toward a future she will not share.

snapshots.name: Latinus
snapshots.body: King of Latium, the region where the Trojans finally make landfall in Italy. Warned by prophecy to marry his daughter to a foreign-born husband, he is inclined to welcome the newcomers Turnus has come to resent.

snapshots.name: Lavinia
snapshots.body: Daughter of King Latinus, whose hand in marriage is claimed by both Turnus and, by the working of prophecy, Aeneas. She says little in the poem, though the war is fought in her name.

snapshots.name: Ascanius
snapshots.body: Aeneas's young son, also called Iulus, who survives the fall of Troy with his father and grandfather. His descendants are foretold to found the line that will one day lead to Rome.
